claims.text: Lightweight HEAs can combine low density with mechanical strength, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance through synergistic lattice-distortion and sluggish-diffusion effects.
Lattice distortion and sluggish diffusion stabilize a single-phase solid solution.
Lattice distortion and sluggish diffusion inhibit the formation of detrimental intermetallic phases.
The proposed initial alloy has a single-phase solid-solution structure.
The proposed initial alloy contains elements with significant atomic-size differences.
Increasing atomic-size mismatch increases lattice distortion.
Lattice distortion increases the energy barrier for dislocation motion.
The increased barrier to dislocation motion enhances mechanical strength.
Sluggish diffusion reduces the kinetics of phase separation.
Reduced phase-separation and oxidation kinetics improve corrosion resistance.
Reduced oxidation kinetics improve high-temperature oxidation resistance.
At otherwise identical conditions, alloys with higher atomic-size mismatch will have higher mechanical strength than the low-mismatch baseline.
At otherwise identical conditions, alloys with higher atomic-size mismatch will have better corrosion resistance than the low-mismatch baseline.
At otherwise identical conditions, alloys with higher atomic-size mismatch will have better high-temperature oxidation resistance than the low-mismatch baseline.
Excessively large atomic-size mismatch destabilizes the single-phase solid solution.
Destabilization caused by excessive atomic-size mismatch leads to brittle intermetallic phases.
The quantitative relationship between atomic-size mismatch and the measured properties may depend on the alloy system.

contradictions.description: The design proposes systematically varying atomic-size mismatch while keeping overall composition constant. For a fixed set of elements and fixed atomic fractions, the usual composition-based atomic-size-mismatch parameter is fixed, so this intervention cannot produce the intended comparison without changing composition, elemental identity, or the definition of mismatch.
